correctness.rationale: Proof establishes the integral normalized Dickson derivative, exact ordinary-branch Hensel isomorphisms, the odd-degree square factorization at both singular input classes, disjointness by Frobenius reduction, and integer fiber counts for every prime p>=5, every unit a and every k>=1. Independently computed polynomial identities for p=5,7,11,13,17 and exhaustively checked 108 modular parameter/exponent cases; finite checks do not replace the all-prime argument. At p=3 an explicit counterexample excludes inappropriate extension.

originality.rationale: The direct 1991 Dickson/Galois-ring article gives ordinary cases plus bounds on the ramified exceptional branches, not the exact p-index all-power singular-ball and fiber classification. The 2023 non-permutation work only bounds generic value sets; the 2021 Dickson work is on finite fields. Comparative searches for Chebyshev equivalence, local branches, and exact image/fiber formulas did not locate a stronger implication. The scanned/author-posted 1991 transcription is imperfect; original priority is not externally certified.
residual_risks: Author-posted transcription of Bremser–Gómez-Calderon has OCR-like degradation in some displayed mathematics; the relevant descriptive statements were readable.
Other unlocated published work may contain an equivalent special-case p-adic theorem. Literature searches are evidence, not proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The characteristic-ramified prime-index case is the natural previously bounded exceptional regime for Dickson maps. Its complete fiber histogram and exact p-adic image measure, including a sharp square/non-square dichotomy and the rare radius-three singular balls, answer an exact local-solubility question uniformly at every power; not a trivial restatement of ordinary Hensel lifting.
